Context: In the `text(1600s)` and `text(1700s)`, many French immigrants settled in Canada. When the French and Indian War broke out, Great Britain took control of the colonies in Canada. In `text(1755)` the French colonists, known as Acadians, were forced to leave their homes. Some returned to Europe, and some settled in other places in the New World. This newspaper article explains what happened when a large group of Acadians came to Louisiana in the `text(late 1700s)`.
Title: Source 3: Adapted from a Newspaper Article about Acadians Who Sailed to Louisiana (1786)
Content: Near the end of `text(last year)`, several large French ships with about `text(one thousand)` Acadian families arrived at New Orleans. The Spanish government gave the Acadians land in different parts of Louisiana. A number of Acadians are also expected to settle in Florida.

Giving the unlucky Acadians land seems like an act of kindness. The Spanish king would consider any such request. However, giving land to the Acadians also prevents Americans from settling on this fertile¹ land.
